classifications.reasoning: The rule detects SMB NULL session connections (Windows NT 1381), which are commonly used for anonymous enumeration of remote systems, shares, and accounts, aligning with Remote System Discovery.
The rule matches SMB directory traversal attempts (CD..), indicating an attempt to explore the file system hierarchy, consistent with File and Directory Discovery.
Similar to the previous rule, this detects a deeper directory traversal pattern (CD...), also indicative of File and Directory Discovery.
The rule identifies Microsoft MSN messenger traffic, which is a policy violation and not an observable ATT&CK technique.
The rule detects ICQ client access via User-Agent, a policy violation with no direct ATT&CK technique mapping.
The rule matches IRC NICK commands, a policy violation for chat usage, not an attack technique.
The rule flags FTP STOR of a 1MB file as a warez indicator; this is a generic file upload and cannot be definitively tied to a specific ATT&CK technique.
The rule flags FTP RETR of a 1MB file as a warez indicator; generic download activity does not map to a specific technique.
The rule detects FTP CWD to root directory, which may indicate file system enumeration, loosely mapping to File and Directory Discovery.

The rule detects FTP MKD . (make current directory), a generic warez indicator with no clear technique mapping.

The rule detects SMTP relay denied messages (550 5.7.1), a mail server configuration issue, not an adversary technique.
